h: Gardens, Minsters and the Dorset Coast
p: Moors Valley sits in a brilliant spot for a weekend of mixed days out. Wimborne Minster is only a short drive away, a handsome little market town with a striking twin-towered minster church and a chained library inside. Just outside Wimborne, Kingston Lacy is a National Trust estate with a grand house, lovely gardens and woodland walks that keep families busy for hours.

If you fancy more heathland and pine, Avon Heath Country Park is close by, a peaceful place with sandy tracks and the chance to spot heathland wildlife. And of course, Bournemouth's long sandy beaches are not far at all, so a treetop morning could easily turn into an afternoon by the sea.

For the Go Ape session itself, a couple of hours is a sensible estimate once you've been briefed and kitted up. Moors Valley can get very busy in the school holidays, so arrive in good time to park, especially if you're also planning to ride the steam railway or use the play trails later in the day.

A few tips for nervous first-timers. Keep three points of contact on the climbs, look at the next platform rather than the ground, and take a breather whenever you need one. The instructors have seen every wobble going, and nobody minds if you take your time.
Bring a change of clothes and a bag for muddy shoes; between the trails and the ropes, you'll probably need them.
